verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              धृष्टद्युम्नं कृपो राजन् वारयामास संयुगे । यथा दृष्ट्वा वने सिंहं शरभो वारयेद्युधि ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O king, Kripa restrained proud Dhristadyumna in the field of battle; even as a Sharva resists a proud lion in the forest, while fighting.

verses.sanskrit: निरुद्धः पार्षतस्तेन गौतमेन बलीयसा । पदात्पदं विचलितुं नाशकत्तत्र भारत ॥२॥
verses.english: O descendant of the Bharata race, the son of Prishata, being thus resisted by the most powerful son of Gautama, was not able to move a step further there (in the battle).
verses.bhavadeepa: धृष्टेति । शरभोष्टपादः सिंहघाती पशुपक्षिशरीरो नृसिंहवत् द्व्यात्मा ॥१॥

verses.sanskrit: गौतमस्य रथं दृष्ट्वा धृष्टद्युम्नरथं प्रति । वित्रेसः सर्वभूतानि क्षयं प्राप्तं च मेनिरे ॥३॥
verses.english: Witnessing the car of Gautama staying by the side of that of Dhrishtadyumna, all the creatures were greatly terrified and considered that destruction was to be attained by him (Dhristadyumna).

verses.sanskrit: तत्रावोचन्विमनसो रथिनः सादिनस्तथा । द्रोणस्य निधनान्नूनं संक्रुद्धो द्विपदां वरः ॥४॥
verses.english: There all the car-warriors and horsemen, who become very inattentive (or gloomy), addressed thus-"This best of persons, the son of Sharadvata, who was possessed of immense prowess and who also was acquainted with the use of celestial weapons and who was, again very high-minded, is sorely filled with anger at the fall of Drona. Will there be escape of Dhrishtadyumna from the hands of Gautama?

verses.sanskrit: शारद्वतो महातेजा दिव्यास्त्रविदुदारधीः । अपि स्वस्ति भवेदद्य धृष्टद्युम्नस्य गौतमात् ॥५॥
अपीयं वाहिनी कृत्स्ना मुच्येत महतो भयात् । अप्ययं ब्राह्मणः सर्वान्न नो हन्यात्समागतान् ॥६॥
verses.english: Will this entire army be freed from that extreme fear? Will not this twice-born person slay us all, who have assembled here?

verses.sanskrit: यादृशं दृश्यते रूपमन्तकप्रतिमं भृशम् । गमिष्यत्यद्य पदवीं भारद्वाजस्य गौतमः ॥७॥
verses.english: Gautama, who exactly appears even like the most dreadful Destroyer himself, will he not obtain today the appellation of the son of Bharadvaja?

verses.sanskrit: आचार्यः क्षिप्रहस्तश्च विजयी च सदा युधि । अस्त्रवान्वीर्यसंपन्नः क्रोधेन च समन्वितः ॥८॥
verses.english: The preceptor (Gautama), who is lighthanded (in the use of weapons) and who is always victorious in battle and who is furnished with various kinds of weapons and who is possessed of immense prowess, is now filled with rage.

verses.sanskrit: पार्षतश्च महायुद्धे विमुखोऽद्याभिलक्ष्यते । इत्येवं विविधा वाचस्तावकानां परैः सह ॥९॥
verses.english: The son of Prishata, too, appears today to have withdrawn from the great battle.' O great king, this and several other speeches were heard to have delivered by the man on your side, as well as by the antagonists; while those two (warriors) assembled there to fight against each other.

verses.sanskrit: व्यश्रूयन्त महाराज तयोस्तत्र समागमे । विनिःश्वस्य ततः क्रोधात्कृपः शारद्वतो नृप ॥१०॥
पार्षतं चार्दयामास निश्चेष्टं सर्वमर्मसु । स हन्यमानः समरे गौतमेन महात्मना ॥११॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O monarch, Kripa, the son of Sharadvata, sighing heavily with rage, struck the son of Prishata, who had lost all his efforts, in all his vital parts.

verses.sanskrit: कर्तव्यं न स्म जानाति मोहेन महताऽऽवृतः । तमब्रवीत्ततो यन्ता कच्चित् क्षेमं तु पार्षत ॥१२॥
verses.english: Having been thus struck in the battle by the high-souled Gautama, he (Dhristadyumna) could not make out what should he do, encompassed as he was by great insensibility.

verses.sanskrit: ईदृशं व्यसनं युद्धे न ते दृष्टं मया क्वचित् । दैवयोगात्तु ते बाणा नापतन्मर्मभेदिनः ॥१३॥
verses.english: Thereupon his charioteer uttered these words to him-'O son of Prishata, it is well with you, perhaps. Such a great calamity was never witnessed by me in the battle, overtaking you?

verses.sanskrit: प्रेषिता द्विजमुख्येन मर्माण्युद्दिश्य सर्वतः । व्यावर्तये रथं तूर्णं नदीवेगमिवार्णवात् ॥१४॥
verses.english: Those shafts, that were capable of piercing through the very vital part and that were shot by the foremost of the twice-born persons, aiming at all the vital parts, had not struck you through the favour of the celestials.

verses.sanskrit: अवध्यं ब्राह्मण मन्ये येन ते विक्रमो हतः । धृष्टद्युम्नस्ततो राजञ्शनकैरब्रवीद्वचः ॥१५॥
verses.english: I will have the car immediately turned back like the current of a river from the great ocean. I consider that the twice-born person is incapable of being slain, by whom you prowess was done away with.

verses.sanskrit: मुह्यते मे मनस्तात गात्रस्वेदश्च जायते । वेपथुश्च शरीरे मे रोमहर्षश्च सारथे ॥१६॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O monarch, Dhristadyumna slowly said these words-'O sire, my mind is being stupefied; and there is perspiration in my limbs. I feel a sensation of trembling in my body; and also the hairs and standing erect upon it.

verses.sanskrit: वर्जयन् ब्राह्मणं युद्धे शनैर्याहि यतोऽर्जुनः । अर्जुनं भीमसेनं वा समरे प्राप्य सारथे ॥१७॥
verses.english: After abandoning the twice-born person in the battle, possessed slowly where Arjuna stays. After having come to the presence of either Arjuna or Bhima in the field, O charioteer, I will surely attain prosperity today. This is my certain belief.

verses.sanskrit: क्षेममद्य भवेदेवमेषा मे नैष्ठिकी मतिः । ततः प्रायान्महाराज सारथिस्त्वरयन् हयान् ॥१८॥
यतो भीमो महेष्वासो युयुधे तव सैनिकैः । प्रद्रुतं च रथं दृष्ट्वा धृष्टद्युम्नस्य मारिष ॥१९॥
verses.english: Thereupon, O powerful king, the charioteer, after having driven the horses, advanced to the place, where that powerful bowman, Bhimasena, was battling with your soldiers.

verses.sanskrit: किरञ्शतशतान्येव गौतमोऽनुययौ तदा । शङ्खं च पूरयामास मुहुर्मुहुररिन्दमः ॥२०॥
verses.english: O sire, Gautama, after witnessing that the car of Dhrishtadyumna was with-drawing from the field, then followed it, shooting hundreds of arrows at it.

verses.sanskrit: पार्षतं त्रासयामास महेन्द्रो नमुचिं यथा । शिखण्डिनं तु समरे भीष्ममृत्युं दुरासदम् ॥२१॥
verses.english: That chastiser of foes blew his conch over and over again, and then he routed the son of Prishata, even as Indra routed Namuchi (a Danava, in the battle of old).

verses.sanskrit: हार्दिक्यो वारयामास स्मयन्निव मुहुर्मुहुः । शिखण्डी तु समासाद्य हृदिकानां महारथम् ॥२२॥
verses.english: The son of Hridika, smiling over and over again, resisted Shikhandin, who was the cause of death of Bhishma and most invincible in the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्चभिर्निशितैर्भल्लैर्जत्रुदेशे समाहनत् । कृतवर्मा तु संक्रुद्धो भित्त्वा षष्ट्या पतत्रिभिः ॥२३॥
verses.english: Shikhandin, however, coming against the mightiest car-warrior of the Hridika race struck him with five sharp and broad-headed arrows at the shoulder-joint.

verses.sanskrit: धनुरेकेन चिच्छेद हसन् राजन्महारथः । अथान्यद्धनुरादाय द्रुपदस्यात्मजो बली ॥२४॥
verses.english: O king, the mighty car-warrior, Kritavarman, indeed, being highly enraged, penetrated through his antagonist with sixty winged arrows and then, smiling for a time, severed his bow with one individual shaft.

verses.sanskrit: तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति संक्रुद्धो हार्दिक्यं प्रत्यभाषत । ततोऽस्य नवतिं बाणान् रुक्मपुङ्खान्सुतेजनान् ॥२५॥
verses.english: Taking up another bow, the most powerful son of Drupada, being greatly enraged, replied to the son of Hridika saying, Wait, Wait.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेषयामास राजेन्द्र तेऽस्याभ्रश्यन्त वर्मणः । वितथांस्तान्समालक्ष्य पतितांश्च महीतले ॥२६॥
verses.english: O lord of kings, then he (Shikhandin) shot at his antagonist ninety arrows, that were furnished with the wings of gold and possessed of great force. But these arrows were shot back from his (Kritavarman's) armour.

verses.sanskrit: क्षुरप्रेण सुतीक्ष्णेन कार्मुकं चिच्छिदे भृशम् । अथैनं छिन्नधन्वानं भग्नशृङ्गमिवर्षभम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Beholding those arrows thus sent back and scattered over the ground, he (Shikhandin) severed his dreadful bow with a sharp, razorhanded shaft.

verses.sanskrit: अशीत्या मार्गणैः क्रुद्धो बाह्वोरुरसि चार्पयत् । कृतवर्मा तु संक्रुद्धो मार्गणैः क्षतविक्षतः ॥२८॥
verses.english: Then having been filled with rage, he struck this one (the son of Hridika), who, with his severed bow, resembled a bull with his broken horns, with eighty different arrows both in the chest and arms.

verses.sanskrit: ववाम रुधिरं गात्रैः कुंभवक्त्रादिवोदकम् । रुधिरेण परिक्लिन्नः कृतवर्मा त्वराजत ॥२९॥
verses.english: Kritavarman, too, who became very angry and who also was greatly wounded by those arrows, vomited blood from his various limbs, as a water-vessel sends forth water through its mouth.

verses.sanskrit: वर्षेण क्लेदितो राजन् यथा गैरिकपर्वतः । अथान्यद्धनुरादाय समार्गणगुणं प्रभुः ॥३०॥
verses.english: even O king, Kritavarman, being thus smeared with blood, blazed forth like a red-chalk mountain streaked (by the streams of liquefied red-chalk) by a shower.

verses.sanskrit: शिखण्डिनं बाणगणैः स्कन्धदेशे व्यताडयत् । स्कन्धदेशस्थितैर्बाणैः शिखण्डी तु व्यराजत ॥३१॥
verses.english: Then the lord (Kritavarman), taking up another bow that was furnished with its string and an arrow, afflicted Shikhandin with the foremost of shafts in the shoulder.

verses.sanskrit: शाखाप्रशाखाविपुलः सुमहान्पादपो यथा । तावन्योन्यं भृशं विद्ध्वा रुधिरेण समुक्षितौ ॥३२॥
verses.english: Shikhandin, indeed, shone most brightly with these shafts, sticking on his shoulders; even as a large tree looks very pretty with its numerous branches and twigs.

verses.sanskrit: अन्योन्यशृङ्गाभिहतौ रेजतुर्वृषभाविव । अन्योन्यस्य वधे यत्नं कुर्वाणौ तौ महारथौ ॥३३॥
verses.english: Those two most powerful car-warriors, who made efforts in slaying each other, whirled round upon their cars, thereby creating thousands of circle, there (in the battle).

verses.sanskrit: रथाभ्यां चेरतुस्तत्र मण्डलानि सहस्रशः । कृतवर्मा महाराज पार्षतं निशितैः शरैः ॥३४॥
रणे विव्याध सप्तत्या स्वर्णपुङ्खैः शिलाशितैः । ततोऽस्य समरे बाणं भोजः प्रहरतां वरः ॥३५॥
verses.english: O great king, Kritavarman pierced the son of Prishata in the battle with seventy sharp arrows, that were furnished with golden wings and also that were whetted on atone.

verses.sanskrit: जीवितान्तकरं घोरं व्यजसृत्त्वरयाऽन्वितः । स तेनाभिहतो राजन् मूर्च्छामाशु समाविशत् ॥३६॥
verses.english: Thereupon the prince of the Bhojas, that foremost of chastisers of foes, shot with great activity at his antagonist a dreadful arrow, that was capable of bringing about the destruction of life, in the field of battle.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वजयष्टिं च सहसा शिश्रिये कश्मलावृतः । अपोवाह रणात्तूर्णं सारथी रथिनां वरम् ॥३७॥
verses.english: O monarch, he, being thus wounded by that arrow, fall into the condition of insensibility; and he, being so choked with stupefaction, suddenly supported himself by holding his flag-staff.

verses.sanskrit: हार्दिक्यशरसंतप्तं निःश्वसन्तं पुनः पुनः । पराजिते ततः शूरे द्रुपदस्यात्मजे प्रभो । व्यद्रवत्पाण्डवी सेना व्यधमाना समन्ततः ॥३८॥
verses.english: Thus his charioteer immediately carried away from the field of battle that foremost of car-warriors, who was highly afflicted by the arrows of the son of Hridika and was sighing repeatedly.
